'''Miguel Alcubierre Moya''' (born March 28, 1964) is a Mexican [[theoretical physicist]].<ref name="Cramer_1997">{{cite web
  | last = Cramer
  | first = John G.
  | authorlink = John G. Cramer
  | title = Alternate View: The Alcubierre Warp Drive
  | url = http://www.npl.washington.edu/AV/altvw81.html
  | work = [[Analog Science Fiction and Fact]]
  | publisher = [[Penny Publications]]
  | accessdate = 22 September 2012
  | date=November 1996
}}</ref>
Alcubierre is known for the proposed [[Alcubierre drive]], a speculative [[warp drive]] by which a spacecraft could achieve faster-than-light travel.

==Personal life==
Alcubierre was born in Mexico City. His father, Miguel Alcubierre Ortiz, a [[Spanish Civil War#Mexico|Spanish refugee]], arrived in Mexico shortly after the [[Spanish Civil War]] with his own father, Miguel Alcubierre Pérez.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/ocio-cultura/2009/04/28/las-siete-vidas-miguel-alcubierre-46212-1361024.html |title = Las siete vidas de Miguel Alcubierre| date=28 April 2009 }}</ref> Alcubierre has three younger siblings, among them is historian Beatriz Alcubierre Moya.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aacademica.org/beatriz.alcubierre |title = Beatriz Alcubierre Moya}}</ref>

From elementary throughout high school, Alcubierre attended [[Colegio Ciudad de México]]. At the age of 13, his father bought him a small telescope, and, together with [[Science fiction|sci-fi]] shows such as ''[[Star Trek]]'', motivated him to pursue a scientific career.<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211211/k78_F-cYIhQ Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20200219074817/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k78_F-cYIhQ Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite AV media| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k78_F-cYIhQ&t=24| title = Ganándole a la velocidad de la luz {{!}} Miguel Alcubierre {{!}} CDI 2016 Play the Game | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref> At the age of 15, after having read [[Patrick Moore]] and [[David A. Hardy|David Hardy]]'s ''[[David A. Hardy#Major books|Challenge of the Stars]]'', Alcubierre decided that he wanted to become an astronomer. He knew that to achieve this he needed to study [[physics]] first.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fundacionunam.org.mx/rostros/miguel-alcubierre-el-fisico-fanatico-de-la-ciencia-ficcion/|title=Miguel Alcubierre, el físico fanático de la ciencia ficción &#124; Fundación UNAM|date=21 May 2020 }}</ref>

==Academic life==
Alcubierre obtained a [[Licentiate (degree)|Licentiate]] degree in [[physics]] in 1988 and a [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree in [[theoretical physics]] in 1990, both at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM). At the end of 1990, Alcubierre moved to Wales to attend graduate school at [[Cardiff University]], receiving his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in 1994 through study of [[Numerical relativity|numerical general relativity]].<ref name="Cramer_1997"/><ref name="Lifeboat_about">{{cite web
  | url = http://lifeboat.com/ex/about
  | title = About
  | publisher = Lifeboat Foundation
  | accessdate = 22 September 2012
}}</ref><ref name="Lifeboat_Alcubierre-bio">{{cite web
  | url = http://lifeboat.com/ex/bios.miguel.alcubierre
  | title = Advisory Board: Dr. Miguel Alcubierre
  | publisher = Lifeboat Foundation
  | accessdate = 22 September 2012
}}</ref><ref>[http://www.nucleares.unam.mx/~soma/miembros/MAlcubierre.htm Biography Miguel Alcubierre Moya] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429211320/http://www.nucleares.unam.mx/~soma/miembros/MAlcubierre.htm |date=2014-04-29 }} - website of the Instituto de Ciencias Nucleares</ref>
After 1996 he worked at the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]] in [[Potsdam]], Germany, developing new numerical techniques used in the description of [[black hole]]s.  Since 2002, he has worked at the Nuclear Sciences Institute of [[UNAM]], where he conducts research in numerical relativity, employing computers to formulate and solve the physical equations first proposed by Albert Einstein.<ref name="career">{{cite web
 |last        = Cansigno
 |first       = Rafael (aka "sigloxiii")
 |url         = http://tenoch.scimexico.com/2008/03/24/cientificos-mexicanos-miguel-alcubierre-moya/
 |title       = Mexican Scientists: Miguel Alcubierre Moya
 |work        = Tenoch
 |format      = [[blog]]
 |date        = 24 March 2008
 |accessdate  = 22 September 2012
 |language    = es
 |url-status  = dead
 |archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120922190342/http://tenoch.scimexico.com/2008/03/24/cientificos-mexicanos-miguel-alcubierre-moya/
 |archivedate = 22 September 2012
}}</ref> 
The [[soliton|solitary wave solutions]] proposed  by Alcubierre for the [[Einstein field equations|Einsteinian field equations]] may possibly  prove general relativity consistent with the experimentally verified [[Locality principle|non-locality]] of [[quantum mechanics]]. This work militates against the idea that quantum non-locality would ultimately require abandoning the mathematical structure of [[general relativity]].{{Citation needed|reason=This is a controversial claim and should be properly cited.|date=December 2025}}

On June 11, 2012, Alcubierre was appointed Director of the Nuclear Sciences Institute at UNAM.

On June 14, 2016, the Governing Board of UNAM re-elected Alcubierre as Director of the Nuclear Sciences Institute for another four-year period.

==May 1994 paper==

While studying for his PhD at [[Cardiff University]]  Alcubierre wrote "The Warp Drive: Hyper-fast travel within general relativity" which was then published in the science journal ''Classical and Quantum Gravity''.<ref name="Warp Alcubierre">{{cite journal |title=The warp drive: hyper-fast travel within general relativity |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |year=1994 |last=Alcubierre |first=Miguel |volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=L73–L77 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/11/5/001 |arxiv = gr-qc/0009013 |bibcode = 1994CQGra..11L..73A |s2cid=4797900 }}</ref>  In this, he describes the [[Alcubierre drive]], a theoretical means of traveling [[faster-than-light|faster than light]] that does not violate the physical principle that nothing can locally travel faster than light. In this paper,  he constructed a [[Metric (general relativity)|model]] that might transport a volume of flat space inside a "bubble" of curved space. This bubble, named as ''Hyper-relativistic local-dynamic space,'' is driven forward by a local expansion of space-time behind it, and an opposite contraction in front of it, so that theoretically a [[spacecraft|spaceship]] would be placed in motion by forces generated in the change made by [[space-time]].

==Media appearances==
Miguel Alcubierre made a special appearance on the TV productions ''[[How William Shatner Changed the World]]''<ref name="IMDB_Alcubierre">{{cite web
  | url = https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3824018/
  | title = Miguel Alcubierre
  | work = [[Internet Movie Database]] (IMDb)
  | accessdate = 22 September 2012
}}</ref>
and [[Michio Kaku]]'s ''Sci Fi Science: Physics of the Impossible'',<ref name="IMDB_Sci-Fi-Science">{{cite web
  | url = https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1588120/
  | title = Sci Fi Science: Physics of the Impossible (2009)
  | work = IMDb
  | accessdate = 22 September 2012
}}</ref><ref name="Nerds_review">{{cite web
  | url = http://nerdsontherocks.com/review-shooter-sci-fi-science-physics-of-the-impossible
  | title = Review Shooter: Sci Fi Science: Physics of the Impossible
  | work = NerdsOnTheRocks.com
  | format = blog
  | date = 19 November 2010
}}</ref>
in which his warp bubble theory was discussed.

Alcubierre has been invited twice to interviews on radio station [[XEEP-AM|Radio Educación XEEP]] (1060 AM), first on February 18, 2011, and later on March 4, 2011, on the technology-related talk show ''Interfase'', where he explained his views on the current state of scientific and technology research in Mexico, and gave a brief introduction to his warp drive model and how it came to be.<ref name="radio-edu-1">{{cite podcast
  | url = http://1060interfase.podomatic.com/player/web/2011-02-21T05_02_17-08_00

  | language=es}}</ref><ref name="radio-edu-2">{{cite podcast
